title: SWING: Balancing Coverage and Faithfulness for Dialogue Summarization
task_boundary: Dialogue-summary coverage and missing-information evaluation versus faithfulness. This is transfer evidence for R2-B, not evidence for Topic segmentation, work-matter assignment, discontinuous Topic spans, or simultaneous Topic labels.
summary: SWING trains a BART-LARGE dialogue summarizer with NLI-derived sentence alignment, an uncovered-content loss, and a contrastive loss. Experiments on SAMSum and DialogSum support improved reference-summary coverage relative to the tested baselines. Human evaluation separates reference-based recall, reference-based precision, and dialogue-grounded faithfulness. The most useful transfer is this separation of evaluation targets and the distinction between missing details and missing sentences. The paper does not establish exhaustive source-content coverage or reliable preservation of business conditions, exceptions, deadlines, evidence, approval constraints, or decision qualifiers.
research_question: Can sentence-level NLI guidance improve coverage of reference summaries while preserving dialogue-summary faithfulness, and which automatic metrics agree with human judgments of these separate dimensions?

datasets.name: SAMSum
datasets.gold_unit: Reference summary associated with a dialogue
datasets.length_statistics: Section 3.1 reports about 94 tokens per dialogue. Appendix A reports 124.1 dialogue words and 23.4 summary words using the NLTK tokenizer. These figures are not reconciled.

datasets.name: DialogSum
datasets.gold_unit: Reference summary associated with a dialogue
datasets.length_statistics: Section 3.1 reports about 131 tokens per dialogue. Appendix A reports 187.5 dialogue words and 31.0 summary words using the NLTK tokenizer. These figures are not reconciled.

dataset_and_gold.units: Dialogue inputs and free-text reference summaries. The method segments summaries into sentences for training alignment.
dataset_and_gold.labels: The reported task uses summary text as supervision. NLI-derived covered/uncovered and matched/unmatched statuses are model-generated training signals, not reported human gold alignment labels.
dataset_and_gold.actually_annotated_for_evaluation: Humans compare two system summaries using win/tie/loss judgments for reference coverage, reference precision, and dialogue faithfulness. The paper also reports manual analyses of missing details, missing sentences, and remaining error categories.
dataset_and_gold.human_evaluation_population: 100 test dialogues from each dataset; CLIFF, CONFIT, and SWING outputs. Appendix B reports eight qualified annotators after screening, but does not specify the number of judgments per pair.
dataset_and_gold.overlap: No overlapping work-matter span labels or simultaneous Topic annotations are reported. Multiple edges in a predicted summary-sentence alignment graph are not evidence of overlapping gold Topic labels.
dataset_and_gold.discontinuity: No discontinuous semantic-span annotation is reported. Group alignment explicitly checks consecutive sentences, so it does not establish arbitrary separated-span prediction.
dataset_and_gold.gold_completeness: Reference summaries specify selected summary content. The paper does not establish that they exhaustively enumerate all important source facts or all business-critical qualifiers.
dataset_and_gold.model_output_capability: The deployed output is a generated summary. The paper does not report inference-time Topic labels, source-span assignments, an omission inventory, or an exhaustive coverage certificate.

key_findings.finding: The empirical task is dialogue summarization on two English datasets. It provides transfer evidence for summary evaluation, not direct evidence for business-email Topic segmentation or assignment.
key_findings.quote: Experiments are conducted on two Englishlanguage dialogue summarization datasets:
key_findings.interpretation_boundary: SAMSum contains online chitchat and DialogSum contains spoken dialogues. Neither reported task predicts concrete work-matter Topics.

key_findings.finding: Human evaluation distinguishes reference-based recall and precision from faithfulness to the source dialogue. Content absent from a reference can therefore reduce reference precision while remaining faithful to the dialogue.
key_findings.quote: examines whether the generated summary is factually consistent with the dialogue.
key_findings.interpretation_boundary: The surrounding definitions at lines 838–843 assign recall and precision to reference-summary content. These are distinct evaluation targets, even though the paper sometimes groups missing information under factual consistency.

key_findings.finding: SWING uses sentence equivalence mappings that can relate one sentence to several sentences, but group matching is restricted to consecutive sentences.
key_findings.interpretation_boundary: Lines 414–420 explicitly restrict the groups to consecutive sentences. This is a predicted alignment between two summaries, not discontinuous source-span representation, simultaneous Topic labeling, or evidence of annotation prevalence.

key_findings.finding: The uncovered loss trains on summaries that combine missing reference sentences with generated sentences judged equivalent to reference content.

key_findings.interpretation_boundary: Lines 446–453 describe recovery relative to the reference summary. The training target cannot explicitly recover an obligation or qualifier that the reference itself omits.

key_findings.finding: SWING improves the reported recall-oriented automatic scores over the listed non-ablation baselines on both datasets, but it does not lead every metric or every ablation comparison.
key_findings.interpretation_boundary: These are aggregate dialogue-summary scores. They do not measure recall of individually labeled conditions, deadlines, exceptions, approval constraints, or Topics. Some ablations have higher recall scores than full SWING.

key_findings.finding: The reported human comparison ranks SWING highest for recall and faithfulness on both datasets, while the text states that SWING is not highest for reference precision.

key_findings.finding: The manual error analysis separates partial loss within a reference sentence from loss of an entire reference sentence. Against CONFIT on 100 SAMSum dialogues, SWING improves 10 missing-detail cases and 6 missing-sentence cases, while introducing those errors in 1 and 2 examples respectively.

key_findings.interpretation_boundary: The definitions and counts span lines 948–966. These are comparative example counts, not recall over an annotated inventory of atomic facts. The paper does not state that the two error categories are mutually exclusive.

key_findings.finding: BARTScore recall has the highest reported correlation with human recall among the tested metrics on both datasets: Kendall's tau of 26.48% for DialogSum and 32.10% for SAMSum.
key_findings.interpretation_boundary: These are correlations after converting metric and human comparisons to lose/tie/win, not coverage percentages or omission-detection accuracy. The results support a candidate transfer metric, not reliable detection of every lost qualifier.

key_findings.finding: The strongest transfer limitation is dependence on reference quality: SWING treats reference content as the basis for both missing-content recovery and training-time consistency judgments, and the authors explicitly caution that the method may fail on datasets with unfaithful references.

metrics.name: ROUGE-L recall
metrics.denominator_or_population: Reference-side sequence content for each evaluated summary pair, aggregated over each dataset's evaluation outputs. Exact evaluated split sizes are not supplied.
metrics.limitations: Lexical summary recall is not semantic recall of required business facts. Full SWING is below some ablations. Only the DialogSum SWING recall value has a significance marker in Table 1.

metrics.name: ROUGE-L F
metrics.target: Bidirectional lexical overlap between generated and reference summaries.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Generated and reference summary content in the evaluated pairs.
metrics.limitations: The paper labels this F1 but describes the F setting generally as an average of directions. The precise formula is not supplied. It is not Topic-assignment F1 or atomic fact recall.

metrics.name: BARTScore recall
metrics.target: Reference reconstruction likelihood as a proxy for semantic coverage.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Evaluated generated/reference summary pairs. The displayed expression is p(S* | S, theta), with S* elsewhere denoting the reference. Token normalization and dataset aggregation are not detailed here.
metrics.limitations: Section 3.2 reverses the S and S* names in its verbal explanation. This is a likelihood score, not a proportion of required facts recovered. Both SWING values carry significance markers, but some ablations score higher.

metrics.name: BARTScore F
metrics.target: Bidirectional summary likelihood or semantic overlap.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Generated/reference summary pairs; the paper describes averaging the two directions.
metrics.limitations: It does not directly measure source-grounded completeness. CONFIT has a higher SAMSum score of -2.188.

metrics.name: FactCC recall
metrics.target: Predicted support for reference sentences using the generated summary as source text.
metrics.denominator_or_population: The stated recall orientation uses reference sentences as claims. The following aggregation description instead refers to sentences within a generated summary, leaving the exact sentence population inconsistent.
metrics.limitations: These percentages are model probabilities, not measured percentages of facts covered. Low correlation with human recall weakens this metric as a coverage validator. The stated sentence population needs clarification.

metrics.name: FactCC F
metrics.target: Bidirectional predicted consistency between generated and reference summaries.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Both summary directions, averaged according to Section 3.2; detailed aggregation inherits the FactCC population ambiguity.
metrics.limitations: This is not an observed factual-accuracy rate. Its reported correlation with human dialogue faithfulness is weak or negative. CONFIT scores higher on SAMSum.

metrics.name: QUALS
metrics.denominator_or_population: Evaluated summaries and internally generated questions and answers. The paper does not specify the exact question population or aggregation formula.
metrics.limitations: The paper reports many invalid generated questions and answers. QUALS is an adjacent factuality metric, not a demonstrated exhaustive missing-information measure. Its strongest reported use here is relative agreement with reference precision.

metrics.name: QAFactEval
metrics.denominator_or_population: Evaluated summaries and the metric's QA procedure; exact question counts and denominator are not reported.
metrics.limitations: This measures an adjacent factuality task rather than the target inventory of missing business information. SWING is below CLIFF on DialogSum and has a significance marker on SAMSum.

metrics.name: Human recall preference
metrics.target: How much reference-summary information a generated summary covers.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Pairwise judgments involving CLIFF, CONFIT, and SWING on 100 test dialogues per dataset. Score equals percentage wins minus percentage losses.
metrics.reported_result: SWING ranks highest on both datasets. Exact scores are not recoverable from the converted Figure 3.
metrics.limitations: Relative preference is not an absolute recall rate. References are selected summaries, not demonstrated exhaustive source-fact inventories. Numbers of judgments per pair and exact score denominators are not stated.

metrics.name: Human precision preference
metrics.target: Whether generated-summary content occurs in the reference summary.
metrics.denominator_or_population: The same pairwise human-evaluation population; percentage wins minus percentage losses.
metrics.reported_result: SWING is not highest on precision.
metrics.limitations: Dialogue-supported content absent from the reference can lower this measure. It must not be interpreted as hallucination-only precision.

metrics.name: Human faithfulness preference
metrics.target: Factual consistency of a generated summary with the original dialogue.
metrics.denominator_or_population: The same pairwise human-evaluation population; percentage wins minus percentage losses.
metrics.reported_result: SWING ranks highest on both datasets. Exact scores are not recoverable from the converted Figure 3.
metrics.limitations: This measures source consistency, not complete source coverage. Pairwise superiority does not establish a zero-error rate.

metrics.name: Inter-annotator agreement
metrics.denominator_or_population: Human annotations from the pairwise evaluation; the averaging procedure and judgment multiplicity are not specified.
metrics.reported_result: Average 'Cohan’s Kappa' of 54.35%, described as moderate agreement.
metrics.limitations: The source spelling is preserved. This is annotation agreement, not summarizer accuracy or coverage.

metrics.name: Kendall's tau with human judgments
metrics.target: Agreement between automatic metric preferences and human preferences.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Automatic and human comparisons converted to {-1, 0, 1}, corresponding to lose, tie, and win, on the Section 4.2 evaluation.
metrics.limitations: These are correlations, not information-recovery percentages. The exact tie rule for continuous automatic scores and uncertainty estimates are not supplied. BARTScore recall leads recall correlation but does not lead every dimension.

metrics.name: Comparative missing-information case counts
metrics.target: Changes in missing details and missing sentences relative to CONFIT.
metrics.limitations: Counts refer to examples with comparative changes. They do not provide a total number of required details, category-specific fact recall, or an established count of unique improved examples across both categories.

metrics.name: Residual error analysis
metrics.target: Remaining summary errors, including missing information.
metrics.denominator_or_population: 100 SAMSum generated summaries compared with references; BART-LARGE is inspected on the same dialogues.
metrics.reported_result: Missing information remains SWING's largest error category. The prose reports 42 BART-LARGE examples with missing information. The converted SWING figure does not reliably map counts to categories.
metrics.limitations: The paper explicitly says this analysis is not comparable with Tang et al. (2022) because the sampled examples differ. It does not report an exhaustive atomic-fact denominator.

metrics.name: Average generated-summary token count
metrics.target: Summary length as a proxy for conciseness.
metrics.denominator_or_population: Generated summaries for each model and dataset.
metrics.limitations: Length alone does not measure redundancy, importance, or coverage. The reported comparison does not isolate whether some coverage gains result from longer output.

metrics.name: NLI model accuracy
metrics.target: MNLI inference classification by the auxiliary RoBERTa-LARGE model.
metrics.denominator_or_population: MNLI evaluation population, not specified in detail.
metrics.limitations: This is a different task from dialogue-summary omission detection and msgloom coverage evaluation. The paper does not establish 91% accuracy for sentence alignment, lost-qualifier detection, or work-email reasoning.

limitations: The datasets and output task do not match business-email Topic segmentation or assignment.
Coverage is anchored to reference summaries. The paper does not demonstrate coverage of source facts that the references omit.
The gold and manual analyses do not separately label conditions, exceptions, deadlines, evidence, approval constraints, or decision qualifiers.
Training-time reference equivalence is a proxy for faithfulness. A generated statement can be supported by the dialogue but absent from the reference.
The many-sentence alignment procedure assumes consecutive sentences and does not establish arbitrary discontinuous grouping.
Human evaluation is a limited pairwise comparison with moderate reported agreement. It does not give absolute completeness rates.
The strongest reported automatic correlation with human recall is 0.321 on SAMSum. No metric is shown to reliably identify every omission.
Missing information remains a major residual problem.
The converted figures do not preserve exact human preference scores or a reliable complete mapping of residual error counts.
The schema file itself was not embedded. Required fields beyond those named in the request cannot be verified without violating the no-tools instruction.
research_gaps: Develop and validate exhaustive source-grounded inventories of business-critical information, independent of whether a reference summary includes each item.
Measure recall separately for conditions, exceptions, deadlines, evidence, approval constraints, and decision qualifiers.
Test automatic omission scores against atomic omission annotations in work email, including faithful summaries that omit critical details.
Evaluate omissions and unsupported additions separately, and retain a distinct category for dialogue-supported content absent from the reference.
Establish model performance and gold annotation prevalence for discontinuous work-matter spans and simultaneous Topic labels using task-matched evidence.
relevance_to_input_code: No code was supplied or inspected. The conceptual transfer is an evaluation design that separates coverage from faithfulness and distinguishes partial-detail omissions from whole-unit omissions. The paper supports testing reference-conditioned scores as auxiliary measures, with human validation and explicit reference-quality limits.

Do not infer that reference-summary coverage equals exhaustive dialogue coverage.

Do not treat Kendall's tau percentages as percentages of information recovered.
Do not treat FactCC probabilities as observed factual-accuracy or coverage rates.
Do not transfer the auxiliary model's approximately 91% MNLI accuracy to omission detection or email reasoning.

Do not treat sentence segmentation used internally for summarization as Topic segmentation.
Do not classify every generated statement absent from a reference as a hallucination.

Do not assume full SWING dominates every ablation or every automatic metric.

Do not infer that the paper's reported improvements generalize to business email without task-matched validation.

Do not assume a verified FactCC claim population or aggregation when comparing its recall or F results across papers.

Do not substitute Figure 1's one-direction entailment diagnostic for the graph's bidirectional matching criterion.

reproducibility.code_statement: Lines 48–49 state that source code is released for research purposes at https://github.com/amazon-science/AWS-SWING.
reproducibility.dataset_statement: Lines 187–192 describe DialogSum and SAMSum as public dialogue summarization datasets.
reproducibility.metrics_statement: Tables 1, 4, 6, and 7 report automatic results or correlations. Human evaluation procedures and qualitative error counts are also reported.
reproducibility.availability_boundary: Availability is based only on the paper's statements. No repository or dataset was accessed. Release of the paper's new human judgments and manual error annotations is not established.
reproducibility.reported_environment: Linux with NVIDIA V100, PyTorch 1.11.0, CUDA 10.1, and Transformers 4.19.2.
reproducibility.remaining_uncertainty: Metric-direction and aggregation inconsistencies, damaged mathematical notation, missing exact human figure values, and unspecified judgments per pair limit exact reconstruction from this text alone.

escalation_reasons: BARTScore recall has a material formula-versus-prose direction conflict. Direction determines whether the metric represents coverage or the reverse relation.
FactCC recall has a material conflict in its sentence population: reference claims versus generated-summary sentences. This affects the interpretation of its reported coverage scores.

Review should preserve the supported qualitative separation between coverage and faithfulness while resolving or explicitly quarantining these metric-definition ambiguities before operational adoption.

adjudications.issue: BARTScore recall direction and inconsistent summary symbols
source_basis: L00223–L00225 Algorithm 1 defines S* as the reference summary and S as the generated summary.
L00649–L00651 The formula is p(S* | S, theta). The prose describes generating the reference given the generated summary but reverses their symbol labels.
adjudications.correction_or_qualification: The formula under Algorithm 1's definitions and the prose's named summary roles agree on reference conditioned on generation. The inconsistency concerns symbol labels; it does not establish two opposing semantic definitions. The executed scoring direction cannot be verified from these windows.
adjudications.synthesis_rule: Describe BARTScore recall conceptually as reference reconstruction conditioned on generation. Retain its reported results under the paper's metric label. Preserve the symbol inconsistency and do not claim implementation verification or exhaustive coverage.

adjudications.issue: FactCC recall claim population and aggregation
source_basis: L00652–L00654 FactCC recall uses a reference sentence as the claim and the generated summary as source text.
L00655–L00656 The aggregation description instead names sentences within a generated summary.
adjudications.correction_or_qualification: These statements specify different sentence populations. The windows do not establish which population produced the reported scores. FactCC F also inherits this uncertainty because it combines both directions.
adjudications.synthesis_rule: Retain FactCC results and correlations as author-reported observations. Do not use them as verified reference-coverage rates or compare them numerically across papers without resolving the claim population and aggregation.

adjudications.issue: F1 labels versus averaging both directions
source_basis: L00618–L00620 The table caption labels F as F1.
L00664–L00667 The metric description says to compute the reverse direction and average both directions.
adjudications.correction_or_qualification: The source supports a bidirectional aggregation description but does not provide a metric-specific equation establishing conventional harmonic-mean F1 for every F-labeled metric. It also does not establish that every implementation departs from conventional F1.
adjudications.synthesis_rule: Use the reported F labels and values. Describe the paper's stated bidirectional averaging procedure without imposing a harmonic-mean or arithmetic-mean formula on every metric.
